It is He who sent down the Book to you from Him: ayats containing clear judgements — they are the core of the Book — and others which are open to interpretation. Those with deviation in their hearts follow what is open to interpretation in it, desiring conflict, seeking its inner meaning. No one knows its inner meaning but Allah. I haven't been signed to Reddit for long enough to know what the old days were like or anything but so far this place seems to be superior in many ways. I'm loving the general layout so far, even on my mobile, although it does still need some work. It would be nice if the webpage resized correctly to my screen like Reddit so that I don't have to use an app but if it ends up being my only choice once there's an app, it's not a train smash.

So far I'm loving the general anti-SJW mood around here. Not to circlejerk about it but I've tolerated these people's bad behavior for a while and now I've had enough. Commenting on Reddit can feel stressful sometimes and I'm looking forward to some actual discussion. If I'm wrong or an asshole about something, tell me, downvote me, allow a conversation to happen, allow me to defend myself or change my mind. I'm here for discussing issues, voicing my views and hopefully learning - not to defend my personal character or life or to have to prove anything about myself to anyone unless I claim to have walked on the moon.

Here's to hoping that people here vote intelligently. I'd love to be able to have a one on one discussion without someone who doesn't like my first comment downvoting every single reply I make thereafter. I'd love to reply to a post asking my opinion about something without being downvoted for my opinion. I know it's just internet points, guess that's just my own personal feelings about it. It's something that can easily deter constructive discussion.

I hope that isn't too much negative, too much ranting about what I don't like on Reddit. This place seems great and I look forward to seeing it grow! Oh, and, hello!

Just beat the campaign last night, and was completely blown away. I first heard about the secret 15 minute way to beat the game when Totalbiscuit was talking about it on a podcast. I thought it was incredible that Pagan actually brings it up at the end, he just asked you to sit at the table and he'd be back to take you to Lakshana....and then the music kicks in "should I stay or should I go", to bring it all together. Just fucking fantastic IMO.

I did not think I was going to enjoy the game as much as I did. Exploring Kyrat, the Yogi and Reggie missions, the Amita/Sabal choices, and Pagan fucking Min made me a believer...and there's still so much content left. I beat the game and I'm at 40%. I took the Sabal route, because I can't think of a 3rd world country that economically relies on heroin/opium that isn't a complete shit hole, and I didn't kill anyone...but now that Pagan is gone I wouldn't mind getting rid of Sabal too and just making Ajay king.

I may have been giving Ubisoft a bad wrap. Moral of the story: Play games outside your comfort zone
